parsed.stack: React Native app for the grandparent (record + hand over) and a plain web link for the grandchild's household - no install on the receiving end. Cloud pipeline: ASR of the 2-minute memory, a text pass to storyboard it into 6 shots, then generated video at ~$0.03/sec, plus voice-preserved narration. Rendering queue on Fly.io, clips on R2. Payment via external web link at 0% platform commission (Stripe), consumable credits.
milestones: Week 1-2: record-and-hand-over flow for a 70-something user: one big button, no editing, no timeline.

Week 3-4: memory-to-storyboard pass and the shot prompt discipline that keeps a consistent look across six clips - inconsistency is what triggers regeneration, and regeneration is the entire cost risk.
Week 5-6: render queue, failure retries, Sunday delivery to a web link, plus the grandchild's reaction going back to the grandparent (the gift loop).
Week 7-8: external-link checkout, credit packs, hard per-account render caps.
Week 9: 15 grandparent/grandchild pairs, measure clips per week and regenerations per clip.
parsed.riskiest_technical_assumption: That a 30-second generated telling lands well enough on the first render - at $0.03/sec a clean 30s clip is $0.90, but a grandparent who rejects and regenerates twice makes it $2.70, and four clips a month at that rate ($10.80) eats a $14.99 credit pack alive; this is exactly the shape that burned $1M/day against $2.1M lifetime revenue.
parsed.cheapest_way_to_test_that_assumption: Hand-produce ten real memories through the generation API yourself, show each to the grandparent who told it, and count how many they would have re-rolled - the average regenerations per accepted clip is the whole business model in one number.
